newsitem.title: USA: Dollar likely near '96 peaks vs yen, mark - Goldman. [CORRECTED 20:37 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely near '96 peaks vs yen, mark - Goldman. [CORRECTED 20:37 GMT]

text.p: The dollar's current rally will probably not extend much past previous 1996 highs near 111 yen and 1.55 marks, according to investment bank Goldman Sachs and Co.
A resurgent Australian dollar could test the $0.8300 level if it breaks past $0.8050, added Goldman in a weekly trading recommendation report. (Corrects number)
The dollar posted fresh eight-week highs against the mark and yen Tuesday, but Goldman analysts in the report predict the rally has neared its zenith.
"Against the mark, a move to the 1.51/1.52 area is likely. Against the yen, a move to test the 110/111 highs of July is possible but not likely to be sustainable," the report reads.
"Beyond September, we are not convinced ... that dollar strength beyond 1.55 marks can occur," the report continues.
The dollar's 1996 highs came on May 28 at 1.5488 marks and on July 8 at 111.19 yen.
Goldman also recommends selling the mark/yen cross rate at its current level near 72.70, with stop-loss bids recommended above 74.10.
Bullish Aussie dollar factors include strong commodity prices and Australian official comments suggesting no monetary policy ease is currently needed, Goldman noted.
"Evidence of a strengthening world economy, pressuring commodity prices, (is) our biggest argument for being bullish the Aussie," the report reads.
